ChainLink 0.3.702

The AI coach was double-counting your rides. It isn't any more — and your data was never wrong.

Please re-download once

If your copy stopped offering updates recently, it can't fetch this one either. An expired access key inside older builds switched the updater off silently. Re-download ChainLink once from this link, drag it to Applications, and you're permanently back on automatic updates. Your data is completely untouched.

If the coach told you your rides were duplicated — please don't delete anything

Two of you reported the coach claiming your rides were logged two or three times, with inflated training load to match (one saw 1700+ TSS for a week). One of you was advised by the coach to go and delete the extra entries.

Nothing was duplicated, and nothing needs deleting. When the same ride arrives from two places — your head unit's file and a service summary, say — ChainLink keeps both but counts only the richer one. Every screen in the app knew that. The coach didn't: it was reading the raw list and seeing each ride more than once.

That's why the number it quoted appeared nowhere else in the app, and why the "duplicates" couldn't be found in your ride list — they were never shown, because they were never counted. The app's own figures were right the whole time. Fixed now, with a test that stops it recurring.

Wellness said two different things at once

The recovery ring and the paragraph underneath it could disagree — one reading "Excellent, go hard", the other "poor, rest today", on the same screen. The ring worked the score out live; the text was reading a copy saved earlier. Everything on that page, including what gets handed to the coach, now uses the same live figure.

"Connected but nothing syncs"

A service that is connected but switched off in Settings → Modules fetched nothing, reported no error, and so got described as "up to date" — freshness the app had never actually checked. It now tells you the service is switched off.

Less repetition, and the Fitness page now explains itself.

The Fitness page explains itself

A new How this is worked out panel under your signature says where each number comes from and — the part worth knowing — what changing your threshold actually does. In short: your FTP drives your zones and the TSS of every ride imported from now on, while rides already scored keep the TSS they were given. Changing it never rewrites your training history.

It also explains why your FTP only ever rises by itself. A breakthrough effort is proof; a quiet month isn't evidence you got slower. If your measured threshold sits below your setting for three weeks, ChainLink proposes a drop and shows you the number — you apply it, in Settings → Training Zones.

Less of the same thing twice

  • Training — the "What this means" paragraph no longer recites the four numbers in the pills directly above it. The interpretation stays; the recital is gone.
  • Fitness — the Performance Management sub-page is removed. It was a second copy of the chart on the Training page, where load and form belong.
  • Fitness — the two threshold numbers in one card (measured now, versus the FTP your zones use) are now labelled so they read as two facts rather than a contradiction.
  • Explanation cards on Training, Fitness and Wellness now start collapsed, showing their first line. Tap to open the full reading — and your choice sticks.

Everything from 0.3.699 is included: a much faster start, the rebuilt iPhone Overview, and printable reports that look the same wherever you make them.

ChainLink 0.3.699

A much faster start, a cleaner iPhone, and printable reports that finally look the same wherever you make them.

Please re-download once

If your copy stopped offering updates recently, it can't fetch this one either. An expired access key inside older builds switched the updater off silently. Re-download ChainLink once from this link, drag it to Applications, and you're permanently back on automatic updates. Your data is completely untouched. Builds from 0.3.686 onward contain nothing that can expire, so this can't happen again.

It starts up fast now

The "Setting things up…" message used to sit on screen for the best part of a minute on a large library. It now clears in a couple of seconds.

Four separate causes, all measured rather than guessed: a hard-coded minimum display time the message couldn't leave before; the message waiting on iCloud's background chatter even when your whole library was already on disk; an awaited Strava network call sitting on the launch path; and breakthrough analysis holding the message while it ran. None of them made the app do anything useful — they just made it say it was busy.

Printable reports

Reports were losing 56pt of page width to a preview-only margin that was never meant to reach the PDF, so tables squeezed and text wrapped raggedly. Fixed. Reports made on an iPhone were also being rendered oversized and clipped — the whole method column of the Bike Fit sheet was falling off the right edge — and they came out on more pages than the same report made on a Mac. A report now looks identical whichever device made it.

iPhone: more room, less repetition

  • Overview — the four metric cards become one Today strip (Form · Fitness · Recovery), plus a compact "Where you're at" block that links through to Rides, Training and Fitness. Fewer cards, same information.
  • Wellness — your recovery score appeared three times on one screen; now once. Smaller hero ring, so the status and advice have room to read properly.
  • Wrapping fixes — long event names, the peak-power grid, the body-metrics row and the planned-ride row no longer wrap or crush.
  • Connection dots only appear when something is actually wrong.

Also

  • Coach insights are generated when you're looking at them rather than at every launch.
  • Bike builds sync properly across devices, and can be exported and shared as a file.
  • Public holidays are respected when generating a plan; test sessions schedule themselves.
